## Where it comes from

The classic female counterpart to
[EN]({{ '/cuneiform/addenda/signs/en/' | relative_url }}) and
[LUGAL]({{ '/cuneiform/addenda/signs/lugal/' | relative_url }}):
*nin* is lady, queen, mistress. It opens goddess names and
queenly titles the way *lugal* opens kingly ones — Ninhursag,
Ninlil, Ninazu, the great ladies of the pantheon.

## How to remember it

The **lady** of the house wears the composed sign: a woman's
title folded into seven tidy wedges. Meet *nin-* at the front of
a name and bow — a goddess or a queen is being introduced.

Piece by piece:

- **nin** — the lady
- **a-zu** — knows the water/seed: the same trusting pattern as
  Diŋir-azu

A name — and a god Ninazu is well known in the pantheon besides.
